items.title: MPS’ double Hail Mary is saner than it seems
items.author: Neil Unmack
items.creator: Neil Unmack
items.summary: To escape a €31 bln raid by Italian giant Intesa, Monte dei Paschi launched bids for rival Banco BPM and wealth group Banca Generali. CEO Luigi Lovaglio needs to persuade his investors, and his M&A targets, that a complex integration will work. A political tailwind may help.
items.body:
The next textbook on M&A tactics should be written by Italian bankers. In the same year that UniCredit (CRDI.MI) CEO Andrea Orcel [USN:L6N4380VE TEXT:"pulled off"] a politically testy coup on Germany's Commerzbank (CBKG.DE) , and Intesa Sanpaolo’s (ISP.MI) Carlo Messina pounced on Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena (BMPS.MI) , the latter’s CEO Luigi Lovaglio has [USN:L1N44H088 TEXT:"come up with"] something totally new. Call it the simultaneous double takeover defence. It looks desperate and complex, but also has a strategic and political logic.
Lovaglio probably doesn’t get much sleep. Last year he [USN:L6N3T10DC TEXT:"clinched"] a hostile takeover of Mediobanca (MDBI.MI) and [USN:L6N40Y15D TEXT:"overturned"] his attempted ousting by a major Monte dei Paschi shareholder.
His current mission is to fend off Italian behemoth Intesa, which in June offered €30.6 billion in cash and stock for the world's oldest bank. Lovaglio's defensive manoeuvre, unveiled on Friday, is to try to acquire smaller rival Banco BPM (BAMI.MI) and also Banca Generali (BGN.MI) , a wealth manager. Before that he will pay his shareholders a €4 billion in special dividends.
Challenge number one will be persuading his M&A targets. The key shareholder for Banca Generali is insurer Assicurazioni Generali (GASI.MI) , in which Monte dei Paschi effectively has a 13% stake. Lovaglio is offering a slim 10% premium. But Generali CEO Philippe Donnet has a reason to play ball. He may be nervous about Intesa, an insurance rival, controlling Monte dei Paschi, because this would also give the banking behemoth significant sway over Generali too.
Winning Banco BPM over looks harder. Lovaglio isn't offering a premium, so roughly 30% French shareholder Crédit Agricole may play hardball. Still, Lovaglio only needs 50% of BPM's shares for that deal to go through. Other investors may be enticed by the synergies.
Then there are Monte dei Paschi's shareholders. Lovaglio needs two-thirds support from his own investors. They include powerful groups like Delfin and Francesco Gaetano Caltagirone. The latter, who owns 10% of Monte dei Paschi, has tussled with the CEO.
At least Lovaglio has a financial case to make. Monte dei Paschi investors will get a €4 billion special dividend and 50.1% of the mash-up that Lovaglio hopes to create. His bank, Banco BPM and Banca Generali were collectively worth €55 billion before the M&A hurricane drove up values, or €51 billion less the special dividend. The union will generate cost savings with a net present value of perhaps €7 billion, according to Breakingviews calculations. On those numbers, the total value to Monte dei Paschi shareholders would be €33 billion.
That compares favourably with the bank's undisturbed €27 billion value. It's also in the same ballpark as the Intesa bid which, using undisturbed prices for comparability and factoring in Monte dei Paschi’s share of the synergies, is worth some €32 billion, per Breakingviews calculations. Aside from the financials, domestic Italian shareholders may also be inclined to support a transaction that fulfills the government’s ambition to create a third force in Italian banking.
One danger is that Intesa's Messina raises his offer. Lovaglio’s complex deal also involves some integration risk, since he has only just swallowed Mediobanca. The 71-year-old will have to keep four sets of employees happy. But as M&A manoeuvres go, you can't fault Lovaglio's ambition.
Follow @Unmack1 on X
Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena on August 21 launched simultaneous all-share takeover bids worth about €34 billion for rival Banco BPM and wealth manager Banca Generali.
The move is part of CEO Luigi Lovaglio's attempt to fend off a hostile takeover approach launched by Italy's largest lender Intesa Sanpaolo, worth €30.6 billion when launched in June.
Shares in Monte dei Paschi were up 0.8% as of 0754 GMT on August 21, while Banco BPM and Banca Generali were down 0.5% and 2.8% respectively.
CONTEXT-NEWS
items.raw_description: To escape a €31 bln raid by Italian giant Intesa, Monte dei Paschi launched bids for rival Banco BPM and wealth group Banca Generali. CEO Luigi Lovaglio needs to persuade his investors, and his M&A targets, that a complex integration will work. A political tailwind may help.

items.title: Singapore's plan to clear forest for housing faces a backlash
items.author: Jun Yong
items.creator: Jun Yong
items.summary: Plans to clear part of Singapore's dwindling secondary forests for high-density housing have sparked a rare public backlash in the city-state, prompting the government to adjust the proposal as it tries to boost housing capacity.
items.body:
(This Aug 21 story has been refiled to remove a withdrawn image.)
Plans to clear part of Singapore's dwindling secondary forests for high-density housing have sparked a rare public backlash in the city-state, prompting the government to adjust the proposal as it tries to boost housing capacity.
Singapore, roughly the size of New York City, said in July it was looking to clear two-thirds of the 23-hectare (57-acre) Maju Forest, an expanse of green in the island's west, to build more public housing.
The announcement triggered an outcry.
More than 49,000 people signed two petitions, urging the government to build on brownfield land, such as golf courses and former commercial and institutional sites, and redevelop older public housing estates at higher densities. More than 700 residents signed a letter to their member of parliament urging Maju Forest to be saved. On Sunday, about 2,000 people joined a rally to show their support for nature and biodiversity, organisers said.
"Stop spending the land (Singapore) can never get back," read one of the petitions.
Last Friday, after closing a public feedback channel on the proposal, the government announced it would make adjustments to retain more greenery than originally planned, but did not provide details.
In a response to a Reuters request for further comments on the plan, the Ministry of National Development shared an August 14 video of Alvin Tan, a junior minister. "We will work out exactly how much more (greenery), but we'll have to accept that this means we can build fewer homes," Tan said in the video.
Like densely populated cities from Hong Kong to London and Sydney, Singapore is grappling with how to meet the housing needs of its population as property prices soar, but, as an island of 744 square kilometres, it has no hinterland where it can expand.
As of 2020, 14% of land in Singapore was used for housing, while 9.3% was parks and nature reserves, according to data from the Urban Redevelopment Authority.
Singapore's population hit a [USN:L3N3VG0BX TEXT:"record 6.11 million people"] as of June last year. It is projected to range from 6.5 million to 6.9 million by 2030.
'CONFLICTING MESSAGES' Maju Forest was once home to a rubber plantation and fruit orchards. Later it was the site of a railway line carrying goods and heavy materials from a nearby shipyard to another station.
But since the train service ended in 1992, the jungle has reclaimed the land and trees have grown and matured, leaving a scenic hiking spot with abandoned rail tracks and a tunnel.
A government commissioned environmental study shows the forest is home to 113 animal species. Among them are the critically endangered straw-headed bulbul — a bird that numbers just 600 to 1,700 worldwide, one-third of them in Singapore — and the Sunda pangolin.
Singapore is expected to clear 7,331 hectares of secondary forests for development, with the future loss of secondary forests 1.2 times the size of all parks and nature reserves in the city-state, according to estimates based on the government's urban plans in a 2023 paper published in science journal MDPI.
Singapore has styled itself as a garden city since 1967, with the city-state's founding father Lee Kuan Yew and political figures regularly planting trees.
Nature Society Singapore President Leong Kwok Peng said authorities gave conflicting messages: "They wanted to plant a million trees and yet at the same time they're removing hundreds and thousands of trees in wild areas." The ministry did not respond to a request for comment.
Rachel Oh, a conservation researcher at the National University of Singapore, said mature forests were able to reduce heat stress at a time when climate change was driving temperatures higher.
"Not all green spaces are equal," she said.
"Mature forests are structurally complex, they are taller, they are bigger, and that's something that a newly planted park could become in maybe 40 to 50 years ... So then when we think about the removal of forests, to me, it's also removal of public health infrastructures."
Nearly 80% of Singaporeans live in government-built flats.
"The overall demand for public housing remains strong ... Not all our housing needs can be met by developing brownfield sites alone," the housing board website said of the site.

items.title: Gold, silver, miners surge as Treasury doubles buybacks
items.author: Scott Spence
items.creator: Scott Spence
items.summary: Falling long-term yields and a weaker dollar lifted precious metals, with leading gold miners gaining nearly 9%.
items.body:
Gold, silver, miners surge as Treasury doubles buybacks

Scott Spence | August 19, 2026 | 5:00 am
Markets   USA   Gold   Silver  

The US Treasury Building in Washington D.C. ( Image courtesy of US Department of Treasury. )

Gold, silver and miners surged Wednesday after the US Treasury unexpectedly said it would at least double purchases of long-dated government debt, pushing down yields and the dollar and giving precious metals a sharp lift.

Spot gold traded around $4,484 an oz. as of 10:25 a.m. ET, up 3.46% from Tuesday’s close, while silver gained 3.33% to about $65.44 an oz. The dollar index dropped 0.78%, while the 10-year Treasury yield declined 1.27% and the 30-year yield fell 1.84%.

Gold miners, which have outpaced the underlying metal this month, posted even stronger gains. The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) jumped 8.8% to about $96.88, Agnico Eagle Mines (TSX: AEM; NYSE: AEM) rose 8.85% to roughly $282.44 and Barrick Mining (NYSE: B; TSX: ABX) advanced 7.66% to $45.33.

The rally shows how sensitive precious metals have become to movements at the long end of the Treasury market. Lower yields reduce the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding gold, while a weaker dollar makes the metal cheaper for buyers using other currencies.

Treasury steps in

The catalyst came from the Treasury rather than the Federal Reserve. Two weeks after publishing its quarterly buyback schedule, the department said Wednesday it was “increasing, by at least double, the size of liquidity support buyback operations” for securities in the 10- to 30-year sector, Bloomberg reported.

The tentative calendar for Sept. 9 through Nov. 4 had indicated purchases of as much as $14 billion. Doubling that amount would imply at least another $14 billion in purchases, with the operations beginning Sept. 9.

The move follows mounting pressure at the long end of the Treasury market. A 10-year auction last week drew the highest financing cost for that maturity since 2007, while a 30-year sale the following day cleared at the steepest yield since 2001, according to Bloomberg. Traders were also preparing for a $16-billion auction of new 20-year bonds.

The Treasury paid about $85 billion in interest to bondholders days earlier, the largest such payment in Bloomberg’s records.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has made clear that he views the 10-year yield as an important measure of his performance.

“My job is to be the nation’s top bond salesman, and Treasury yields are a strong barometer for measuring success in this endeavour,” Bessent said last November.

He has separately said he wants the 10-year yield to carry a “3” handle, meaning below 4%, Reuters reported this month.

Staying power

Whether larger buybacks can keep long-term yields lower remains uncertain. Bloomberg macro strategist Cameron Crise said the additional buying alone is unlikely to reverse long-end selling, although the Treasury’s signal could encourage further short-covering.

Jack McIntyre, a portfolio manager at Brandywine Global Investment Management, compared the move with a version of Operation Twist, the Federal Reserve strategy that sought to lower longer-term borrowing costs by altering the maturity profile of its holdings.

McIntyre told Bloomberg that a slowing economy or a resolution of the Iran conflict would ultimately be more powerful forces for pulling long-term rates lower.

For gold and silver investors, the immediate effect was clearer: Treasury intervention relieved pressure from two of precious metals’ biggest headwinds — elevated long-term yields and a strong dollar — while miners amplified the metals’ gains.

(With files from Bloomberg)

items.title: China Completes First Stage of Work at Disputed South China Sea Reef, Images Show
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: By Greg Torode China has completed the first phase of construction on Antelope Reef in the Paracels archipelago, building a man-made island in the hotly disputed South China Sea that analysts say will form part of its largest military base. Satellite images reviewed by Reuters show the reclaimed …
items.summary_source: The China-Global South Project source metadata
items.body:
By Greg Torode

China has completed the first phase of construction on Antelope Reef in the Paracels archipelago, building a man-made island in the hotly disputed South China Sea that analysts say will form part of its largest military base.

Satellite images reviewed by Reuters show the reclaimed feature in outline for the first time, with barges and dredgers having left after at least six months of work in the busy waterway.

The completion shows the South China Sea as an increasingly militarised arena of competition between China and the United States and its allies, as both sides jostle for advantages that could prove critical in any future conflict over  Taiwan .

“The northern part of the South China Sea would be particularly important in a Taiwan conflict scenario, so Antelope is ideally placed,” said Ben Lewis, founder of the open-source data platform PLATracker.

Construction of buildings has started at the southeast corner of the island, including a helicopter pad, in the July 19 images taken by Vantor, a commercial provider of satellite imagery.

China’s defense ministry did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

China has yet to acknowledge construction of a new military base, while state media have said Antelope will serve civilian needs such as weather forecasting and scientific research.

Likely to Strengthen China’s Military Hold

Regional security analysts and military attaches say it is more likely to strengthen China’s military hold on the northern part of the vital waterway.

The images show a reclaimed island nearly 6 km (4 miles) long, with a straight line of coast longer than 3 km (2 miles) that some analysts see as a potential runway.

A wharf stretching 680 meters fronts a deep-water harbor, with one Vantor image showing a coast guard ship alongside.

In a study this week, the Washington-based Center for Strategic and International Studies said the first excavation work for a new runway appeared to have already started.

Open source intelligence tracker Damien Symon, who first highlighted dredging at the reef on X in early January, said he spotted initial signs of work last December.

Lewis said he believed Antelope Reef could prove to be one of the Chinese military’s most important features in the South China Sea, larger than neighboring Woody Island and easier to defend than a network of bases further south in the Spratlys archipelago.

“I think the importance of the South China Sea and the Southern Theater Command has been elevated in the last year by the Central Military Commission largely as it relates to Taiwan,” Lewis added, referring to China’s top military panel, headed by President Xi Jinping.

Keeping Bombers Closer to the Mainland

China’s military planners might feel more comfortable keeping some weapons, such as its H-6 strategic bombers, in the Paracels, closer to the Chinese mainland, rather than in the Spratlys, farther south.

The construction work was “modest”, Chinese South China Sea scholar Ding Duo said in an opinion piece published in the official China Daily in June.

“Rather than militarisation, the purpose is peaceful and constructive – making the waters safer for everyone who depends on them,” Ding wrote.

The comments mirror China’s previous explanations of its build-up in the Spratlys in waters also claimed by Southeast Asian neighbors Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia, Taiwan and Brunei.

Woody Island has served as the traditional administrative center for China in the South China Sea, housing at times jet fighters and surface-to-air missiles. Triton Island, also in the Paracels, hosts extensive long-range surveillance devices.

China has occupied all the Paracels since 1974, when it forced off the navy of the former South Vietnam. Vietnam, which claims the entire grouping as its own, has in recent years moved to expand its network of bases in the Spratlys.

Vietnam’s foreign ministry did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. It has previously asserted its sovereignty over Antelope, saying in March that it “resolutely opposes such actions (and) has made representations”.

Antelope could also help support any bid by China to create so-called bastions or protected ocean areas in the South China Sea to defend its nuclear-armed ballistic missile submarines, said Singapore-based security scholar Collin Koh.

Koh said the island buildup, likely to house extensive surveillance equipment, could complicate submarine operations by the United States and Vietnam, both of which are active in the area.

Such bastions close to home ports would protect China’s submarines from exposure to rival attacks, avoiding the need to send them out into the western Pacific.

Some analysts believe the South China Sea was chosen for China’s  test firing last month  of a long-range missile from a submarine.

Once complete, the Paracels facilities would strengthen China’s ability to monitor the United States and allies in peacetime, and add complexity in a conflict, said Carl Thayer, a professor at the Australian Defense Force Academy.

“It’s one more thing the United States would have to take care of, and something they could attempt to defend from the Chinese mainland.”

items.title: China’s July Coal Output Falls to Pandemic-Era Levels in Wake of Deadly Accident
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: By Colleen Howe China’s coal output in July fell back to pandemic-era levels, statistics bureau data showed on Monday, as stepped-up safety oversight after a deadly mining accident continued to weigh on mining operations. Coal output in China, the world’s largest producer, fell 10.1% to 343.21 …
items.summary_source: The China-Global South Project source metadata
items.body:
By Colleen Howe

China’s coal output in July fell back to pandemic-era levels, statistics bureau data showed on Monday, as stepped-up safety oversight after a deadly mining accident continued to weigh on mining operations.

Coal output in China, the world’s largest producer, fell 10.1% to 343.21 million metric tons in July from a year earlier, the National Bureau of Statistics said.

That was the lowest standalone monthly output figure reported since September 2021. That excludes output for the months of January and February, which are reported as a combined figure to smooth out the effects of the Lunar New Year holiday, which falls in either month and also affects production.

“This round of production declines was not caused by a weakening in demand, but rather stemmed from the continuous tightening of domestic coal mine safety regulations,” analysts at Galaxy Futures said in a note.

In May, 82 people were killed in a gas explosion at the Liushenyu mine in Shanxi province, the deadliest mining accident in 17 years, forcing many mines in the coal-rich province to close for inspections.

An initial probe into the incident found that the mine was using hidden tunnels and fake doors to shield some areas of the mine from regulatory oversight, state media reported.

“Many mines have voluntarily reduced their production loads after resuming operations, with significant reductions in Shanxi province in particular,” the Galaxy Futures analysts said.

The analysts forecast a 7%-9% year-on-year drop in August coal production and a 3%-5% decline for the full year, as tighter scrutiny forces mines to curb their previously undisclosed production.

Output for January-July reached 2.7 billion metric tons, down 2.9% compared with the same period last year, the statistics bureau data showed.

(Reporting by Colleen Howe; Editing by Sonali Paul and Emelia Sithole-Matarise)

items.summary: L'Europe vue en hausse, Washington annonce une offensive économique contre Téhéran
items.body:
L'Europe vue en hausse, Washington annonce une offensive économique contre Téhéran
25 août (Reuters) - Les principales Bourses européennes sont attendues en hausse mardi à l'ouverture, regagnant du terrain après leurs pertes de la veille, tandis que les investisseurs digèrent l'avertissement américain à l'encontre des pays qui continuent de faire des affaires avec l'Iran et attendent les résultats de Nvidia pour rééquilibrer leur appétit pour la technologie.
Shein-L'IPO à Hong Kong, d'un montant de $1,8 mld, est intégralement souscrite-sources
Le carnet d’ordres de l’introduction en Bourse (IPO) de Shein à Hong Kong, visant à lever jusqu'à 1,8 milliard de dollars (1,54 milliard d'euros), a été intégralement couvert, ont déclaré deux sources proches du dossier.
La "guerre de Trump" à l'origine de la flambée des taux obligataires - ministre allemand
BERLIN, 24 août (Reuters) - La récente flambée des taux obligataires est le résultat de "la guerre menée par le président américain Donald Trump en Iran", a déclaré lundi le ministre allemand des Finances Lars Klingbeil, lors d'une conférence de presse à Schaan, au Liechtenstein.
Trump menace d'imposer des droits de douane de 50% sur les véhicules produits au Canada
WASHINGTON, 24 août (Reuters) - Les droits de douane américains sur les voitures, les camions, les pièces détachées automobiles et l'acier produits au Canada seront portés à 50% à compter du 1er janvier 2027, a déclaré lundi Donald Trump dans un message publié sur les réseaux sociaux après l'échec des négociations commerciales avec Ottawa.
Les valeurs à suivre à Wall Street
Principales valeurs à suivre lundi à Wall Street, où les contrats à terme sur les principaux indices suggèrent une ouverture stable (-0,01%) pour le Dow Jones <.DJI>, en baisse de 0,12% pour le Standard & Poor's-500 <.SPX> et de 0,49% pour le Nasdaq.
Jackson Hole: Le premier discours de Warsh sous surveillance avec l'agitation sur l'obligataire
WASHINGTON, 24 août (Reuters) - Le discours de Kevin Warsh, président de la Réserve fédérale américaine (Fed), lors de la conférence de Jackson Hole qui débute cette semaine, suscitera sans aucun doute un intérêt allant bien au-delà de l'évidence, à un moment où le marché cherche des éclaircissements sur la récente flambée des rendements obligataires et des garanties quant à l'indépendance de la banque centrale.
Le milliardaire allemand Klaus-Michael Kuehne s'éteint à l'âge de 89 ans
Le milliardaire allemand Klaus-Michael Kuehne, actionnaire majoritaire du groupe logistique suisse Kuehne+Nagel, est décédé à l'âge de 89 ans, a annoncé lundi la société.
Volkswagen: Les salariés inquiets de la communication du directoire
Les salariés de Volkswagen ont critiqué ce qu’ils ont qualifié de "communication externe désastreuse" de la part du directoire, alors que le plus grand constructeur automobile européen envisage de nouvelles réductions de coûts, selon un article interne du comité d’entreprise consulté lundi par Reuters.
Shein pourrait atteindre une valorisation de $27 mds lors de son IPO à Hong Kong
La valorisation de Shein a chuté d'environ 70% par rapport au pic de près de 100 milliards de dollars atteint lors d'un tour de table effectué il y a quatre ans, alors que le géant en ligne chinois de la mode éphémère entend lever jusqu'à 1,77 milliards de dollars en vue de son introduction en Bourse à Hong Kong.
Shell: Les actifs chimiques américains suscitent l'intérêt d'Exxon et LyondellBasell selon le Financial Times
Shell a suscité l'intérêt de plusieurs acquéreurs potentiels, dont ExxonMobil et LyondellBasell, pour ses actifs chimiques américains, qui pourraient atteindre une valeur de 8 milliards de dollars (6,85 milliards d'euros), a rapporté lundi le Financial Times (FT).
